chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Muhassin ibn Ahmad from Aban said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever is in a hurry and prays the Salat of Ja'far exclusively, then completes the tasbih while going about his needs.'

key_terms.التَّسْبِيحَ: The Tasbih, referring to the specific glorifications associated with this prayer
key_terms.حَوَائِجِهِ: His needs/affairs, referring to daily activities or travel
key_terms.صَلاَةَ جَعْفَرٍ: Salat of Ja'far, a specific prayer attributed to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.مُجَرَّدَةً: Exclusively/Solely, indicating this prayer is performed on its own

ai.seo_question: How can one complete the Tasbih of Ja'far while traveling or busy?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential flexibility (rukhas) within Shia practice, allowing the 'Salat of Ja'far' to be performed in two parts: the obligatory units (rak'ahs) and the subsequent glorifications (tasbihat). It specifically addresses the needs of travelers or those pressed for time, permitting the recitation of the lengthy tasbih segments to be completed while walking or attending to other affairs, thereby emphasizing ease in worship without compromising the prayer's structure. This ruling is central to the Shia understanding of how to maintain devotional consistency amidst the demands of daily life and travel.
